subject.title: Memory/QMD: isolate mcporter sidecars per agent

question: Should OpenClaw permanently classify bare QMD stdio definitions as generated per-agent state while retaining every definition with auth, environment, lifecycle, logging, remote, cwd, or path semantics in its original MCPorter config?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but this classifier changes existing users' configuration source, daemon identity, and memory-index routing; repository policy requires an area owner to accept that upgrade contract rather than deriving product intent from tests.

options.title: Approve the ownership split
options.body: Adopt the current generated-versus-external rule, then rebase and merge only after exact-head checks and upgrade proof pass.

options.title: Narrow to environment isolation
options.body: Land only the smaller QMD-versus-MCPorter process-environment repair and defer generated configuration ownership to a separate design.

options.title: Pause the integration change
options.body: Keep existing behavior until maintainers define a different canonical MCPorter configuration and daemon ownership contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the ownership split
recommendation.body: Adopt the current generated-versus-external rule, then rebase and merge only after exact-head checks and upgrade proof pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work and tests make this person the strongest available routing candidate for the current QMD memory behavior.
